The Nightmare on Elm Street Mandela Effect Nobody Spotted

short // Jun 22, 2026 · Updated Sep 24, 2026

Watch on YouTube

For years, I was convinced Cathy Dennis's "Touch Me (All Night Long)" was in A Nightmare on Elm Street Part 2: Freddy's Revenge. I would've bet money on it.

I was wrong. And the way I got it wrong is kind of fascinating.

How my brain rewrote a horror movie

I saw Freddy's Revenge as a kid once or twice, then didn't watch it again until the early 2000s. In between, I heard Cathy Dennis's version of "Touch Me (All Night Long)" so many times that my brain quietly stitched the two memories together.

So when I finally rewatched the movie, the song didn't sound like the version in my head. I was like, "What in the dream warrior is this?"

The timeline doesn't lie

The dates make it impossible:

  • Freddy's Revenge came out in 1985.
  • Cathy Dennis's version came out in 1991.

The song in the movie is the original "Touch Me (All Night Long)" by Wish featuring Fonda Rae, from 1984. It's the track Jesse dances to in that famous scene where he's unpacking and cleaning up his room. Cathy Dennis's cover came six years after the movie.

My memory didn't just fade. It swapped in a recording that didn't even exist yet.

Two versions, two different vibes

Both versions are bangers, but they don't have the same energy.

The Wish and Fonda Rae original is mid-'80s club music: synth-heavy, with Fonda Rae's big vocal out front. It reached number 5 on Billboard's dance club chart and number 49 in the UK.

Cathy Dennis's version is glossy early-'90s dance-pop, and it was a much bigger hit. It went to number 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 in May 1991 and number 1 on the dance club chart. That's the version that was all over the radio, which is exactly why it overwrote the original in my head.

So is it really a Mandela effect?

A Mandela effect is usually a false memory that a lot of people share. I can't prove this one is widespread, which is why I'm asking. But on a personal level, it's the same thing: a confident memory built out of two different sources.

And it makes sense that it happened with this movie. Freddy's Revenge is the odd one out in the Nightmare series, and that dance scene is one of the most talked-about moments in it. A scene that memorable, paired with a song that later became a bigger hit in a different version, is the perfect setup for your brain to mix things up.

Update (September 2026)

Freddy's coming back. In July, Paramount announced a new A Nightmare on Elm Street movie after making a deal with Wes Craven's estate for the U.S. rights. It's based on the original 1984 film and comes from Paramount Primal, the studio's new horror label run by J.D. Lifshitz and Raphael Margules, the producing team behind Barbarian and Weapons. Craven's widow, Iya Labunka, and his son, Jonathan Craven, are producing. There's no release date yet.

Sources: Variety, The Hollywood Reporter, Wikipedia: Touch Me (All Night Long))

Quick answers

What song is in A Nightmare on Elm Street 2: Freddy's Revenge? "Touch Me (All Night Long)" by Wish featuring Fonda Rae, the 1984 original, plays in the scene where Jesse dances while cleaning up his room.

Is Cathy Dennis's "Touch Me (All Night Long)" in Freddy's Revenge? No. Her cover came out in 1991, six years after the movie.

When did Freddy's Revenge come out? In 1985.

How high did Cathy Dennis's "Touch Me" chart? It reached number 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 in May 1991.

Is there a new Nightmare on Elm Street movie? Yes. Paramount announced one in July 2026, based on the 1984 original, but there's no release date yet.

Your turn

Which version sounds right to you: Wish and Fonda Rae, or Cathy Dennis? And be honest: does the Cathy Dennis version feel more right than the original? Drop your answer in the comments.
